Chapter 3: Crime, Data, and the Unexpected Truths Behind Social Change
Let’s dive into a topic that never fails to spark strong emotions—crime. Maybe it’s fear, maybe anger, or even a hope that justice will somehow prevail.
Politicians love to promise tough action on crime, police roll out new strategies, and communities worry about safety. But, what if the real story behind changes in crime rates isn’t what anyone expects?
Think back to the early 1990s—American cities felt almost out of control. Experts were sounding the alarm, predicting things would just keep spiraling. Then, almost overnight, everything changed. Crime rates dropped, and not just a little—they plummeted.
People scrambled for answers. Was it smarter policing? A booming economy? Tougher prison sentences? Everyone had a theory.
But here’s where it gets interesting. When researchers started digging into the data, those usual explanations didn’t really add up. The timing was off. Cities that hadn’t switched up their policing saw the same dramatic drops.
So what was really going on?
The answer, believe it or not, was rooted in a decision made decades before. Back in the early 1970s, a landmark court case made abortion legal throughout the United States. Suddenly, women who weren’t ready—or able—to raise a child had a choice.
Over the following years, fewer children were born into situations that made life much tougher: poverty, family instability, or not having enough support.
By the time these children would’ve reached their late teens and early twenties—the age when crime is most likely to happen—their absence started showing up in the statistics.
Fewer at-risk kids meant fewer young adults who might get pulled into crime. It wasn’t obvious at first, and it definitely challenged what a lot of people believed about the root causes of crime.
Not everyone was comfortable with this discovery. It forced some tough questions—about the ripple effects of social policies and the limits of traditional thinking. But the data was hard to ignore: sometimes, the biggest changes come from places nobody’s watching, and the truth is buried deeper than we’d like to admit.
And this isn’t the only case where data has flipped the script. Take one city’s strategy: police tried cracking down on small, visible offenses—stuff like vandalism or skipping out on subway fares. The idea was, stop the little crimes, and you’ll prevent bigger ones.
But the results? They were mixed. Turns out, the connection between police tactics and crime rates is a lot messier than it looks on the surface.
So, what can we take from all this? Our world is full of hidden connections. The obvious answer isn’t always the right one, and sometimes, the real story only comes out when we’re willing to look beyond what everyone assumes.
When we dig deeper, ask better questions, and trust the data, we might just uncover the real forces shaping our society—often in ways we’d never expect.
